expeditions.title: 43rd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica (43-ISEA)
expeditions.institution: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)
expeditions.vesselOrBase: MV Vasiliy Golovnin & Stations Maitri / Bharati
expeditions.publicSummary: The 43rd ISEA successfully completed major cryospheric drilling, paleoclimatic ice-core retrieval in Central Dronning Maud Land, atmospheric aerosol sampling, and preparatory geo-technical surveys for the upcoming green-energy Maitri-II station.
scientificObjectives: Paleoclimate reconstruction via shallow ice cores from Amery Ice Shelf and DML
Geomagnetic pulsations and auroral electrojet mapping at Maitri & Bharati
Microbial diversity and extremophile bioprospecting in Schirmacher oasis water bodies
Pre-construction soil mechanics and seismic baseline for Maitri-II modern base

assets.title: 43rd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica: Comprehensive Technical and Scientific Report
assets.abstract: Authoritative consolidated expedition report detailing 43-ISEA scientific achievements across Maitri and Bharati stations, including ice core drilling in Dronning Maud Land, meteorological observations, upper atmospheric physics, and site surveys for the Maitri II modern polar station.
assets.spatialCoverageName: Schirmacher Oasis and Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica
assets.rightsHolder: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt. of India)

versions.extractedText: 43rd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica (2023-2024) Executive Summary: The expedition achieved 100% of planned scientific milestones. At Maitri station (70°45'S, 11°44'E), deep ice drilling reached 120 meters depth revealing aerosol deposition patterns across the late Holocene. At Bharati station (69°24'S, 76°11'E), high-frequency ionospheric radar operated continuously for 94 days capturing severe geomagnetic storm perturbations. Modernisation surveys for Maitri II confirmed low-permafrost bedrock stability at Site Bravo with renewable solar-wind microgrid feasibility.

assets.title: Maitri Station Decadal Surface Meteorological Time-Series (2014–2024)
assets.abstract: Continuous hourly automatic weather station (AWS) surface meteorology observations from Maitri Station, Schirmacher Oasis. Parameters include 2-meter air temperature, surface atmospheric pressure, wind speed at 10m, wind direction, relative humidity, and global solar radiation.

accessPolicy.policySource: Open Government Data (OGD) / NPDC Open Access

datasetDetail.methodology: Automated 1-minute digital sampling integrated into 1-hour WMO standardized records. Despiked and verified against manual psychrometer observations.
datasetDetail.qualityControlNotes: Calibrated annually during austral summer expedition changeovers. Missing sensor intervals flagged with code -999.0.

assets.title: 12th Indian Southern Ocean Expedition: Hydrographic CTD Cruise Summary and Biogeochemistry Report
assets.abstract: Cruise summary and hydrographic findings from the 12th Southern Ocean Expedition aboard ORV Sagar Nidhi. Documents CTD profiles to 3500m across the Polar Front (53°S), chlorophyll-a maxima, carbon export flux measurements, and trace metal clean seawater sampling.
assets.spatialCoverageName: 57°E Meridian Transect (Sub-Antarctic Zone to Coastal Antarctica)
assets.rightsHolder: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research

accessPolicy.policySource: NCPOR Southern Ocean Program Data Charter

versions.extractedText: 12th Southern Ocean Expedition (SOE-12) Findings: A high-density hydrographic transect along 57°E revealed a southward migration of the Sub-Antarctic Front by 0.8 degrees compared to 2018 baselines. Deep chlorophyll maximum (DCM) was observed at 75-90 meters depth in the Polar Frontal Zone, dominated by diatom taxa Fragilariopsis kerguelensis. Export flux measured via thorium-234 deficiency indicated enhanced carbon drawdown of 42 mmol C/m²/day.

assets.title: Aurora Australis Glow over Bharati Station, Larsemann Hills
assets.abstract: High-altitude atmospheric electromagnetic excitation producing intense emerald and violet auroral ribbons directly above the main architectural dome of India's Bharati Station during the austral polar night.

assets.title: Glacial Recession Dynamics in the Chandra Basin from Himansh High-Altitude Observatory
assets.abstract: Documentary footage and field time-lapse tracking ice thinning, crevassing, and meltwater channel formations on the Sutri Dhaka benchmark glacier in the Western Himalayas.

versions.extractedText: Transcript [00:00-00:35]: Welcome to Himansh, India's highest glaciological research station at 4,080 meters above sea level in the Chandra basin. [00:35-01:10]: Here, our team uses ground penetrating radar and ablation stakes to measure ice loss on the Sutri Dhaka glacier. [01:10-02:22]: Over the past two decades, warming summer temperatures have accelerated snout retreat to approximately 18 meters per year, directly altering downstream water availability in the Indus-Ganges headwaters.

contentDrafts.title: Unlocking Antarctic Secrets: How 43-ISEA Drilled 120m into Ancient Ice
contentDrafts.generatedHeadline: ❄️ Journey to the Bottom of the Earth: Inside India's 43rd Antarctic Mission!
contentDrafts.generatedBody:
Did you know that ice sheets in Antarctica act like frozen time machines? During the 43rd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica (43-ISEA), Indian scientists at Maitri Station drilled 120 meters deep into the continental ice sheet! Each layer of trapped air bubbles tells us what Earth's atmosphere was like thousands of years ago.

While temperatures dropped below -18°C with biting katabatic winds exceeding 28 knots, our scientists operated sophisticated lasers and sensors to measure atmospheric dust and green auroras dancing over Bharati station.
bulletPoints: Maitri Station is located in the Schirmacher Oasis at -70.767°S, 11.733°E
Ice cores preserve ancient atmospheric air samples from centuries ago
Bharati station tracked auroral electrojets continuously for 94 days
All data is preserved according to international FAIR data stewardship
